title: pvMandelbrot
body:
## pvMandelbrot

Generates image data whose float point scalar "Iterations" counts the iterations of z → z² + C before |z| exceeds 2 (capped at MaximumNumberofIterations). The 4-D parameter space (C real, C imaginary, X real, X imaginary, where X is the starting z) is sampled from OriginCX over SizeCX, with ProjectionAxes choosing which three parameters map to the image x, y and z axes. Use it as a synthetic image or volume with fine detail for testing.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- The native description calls the values unsigned char; VTK produces float values.
- The output's origin and spacing are in Mandelbrot parameter units, not physical coordinates.
- Schemaxis generates this source from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for it, so inspect the output before relying on it.

Native constructor: `Mandelbrot`. Identity: `sources/ImageMandelbrotSource`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

No connected inputs (source/resource).


### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `MaximumNumberofIterations` | The value of this property specifies the limit on computational iterations (i.e., the maximum number of iterations to perform to determine if the value will go above 2). Values less than 2.0 after the specified number of iterations are considered in the fractal set. | `{"maximum":5000,"minimum":1,"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `OriginCX` | The four values of this property indicate (in order) the components of C (real and imaginary) and the components of the initial value, X (real and imaginary). | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":4,"minItems":4,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1,1]` |
| `ProjectionAxes` | The three values in this property allow you to specify the projection from the 4D space used by the Mandelbrot set to the axes of the 3D volume. By default, the real component of C (represented by 0) is mapped to the X axis; the imaginary component of C (represented by 1) is mapped to the Y axis; and the real component of X, the initial value (represented by 2) is mapped to the Z axis. The imaginary component of X is represented by 3. All values entered must be between 0 and 3, inclusive. | `{"items":{"maximum":3,"minimum":0,"type":"integer"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[0,0,0]` |
| `SizeCX` | The four values of this property indicate the length of the output in each of the four dimensions (the real and imaginary components of C and the real and imaginary components of X). The three dimensions specified in the Projection Axes property will determine which of these values specify the length of the axes in the output. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":4,"minItems":4,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1,1]` |
| `SubsampleRate` | This property specifies the rate at which to subsample the volume. The extent of the dataset in each dimension will be divided by this value. | `{"minimum":1,"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `WholeExtent` | The six values in the property indicate the X, Y, and Z extent of the output data. The first two numbers are the minimum and maximum X extent; the next two are the minimum and maximum Y extent; and the final two are the minimum and maximum Z extent. The numbers are inclusive, so values of 0, 250, 0, 250, 0, 0 indicate that the dimensions of the output will be 251 x 251 x 1. | `{"items":{"type":"integer"},"maxItems":6,"minItems":6,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1,1,1,1]` |
